prompt.context: One of the many functions of the New York State Health Commission is to coordinate organ donation amongst the state's many hospitals. In recent years the demand for organs has been greater than the supply. As a result, many patients die each year because there are not enough organ donations. The Health Commission has hired McKinsey to help it determine how to increase the number of annual organ donations in New York. For the purposes of this case, assume that only New York residents are involved as donors and recipients.
prompt.question: How can the New York State Health Commission increase the number of annual organ donations in New York?

clarifying_info.q: How does the organ donation registration process work in New York?
clarifying_info.a: In New York, organs will be harvested from terminally ill or injured patients just before death only if they are a registered organ donor or if the hospital receives permission from the next of kin. New York residents may choose to register as organ donors when they apply for a driver's license.

exhibits.title: Customer Segmentation Data
exhibits.shows: A table showing registered donors (in millions) and total population (in millions) broken down by four demographic segments: Caucasian, African-American, Hispanic, and Other.

framework: Identify factors and drivers of organ donation volume (equation-based decomposition)
Quantify the registered-donor rate required to meet kidney demand (math)
Brainstorm strategies to increase registered donors
Analyze segmentation data to identify the best target demographic
Develop targeted tactics for the chosen segment
Deliver a short, firm recommendation to leadership

questions.prompt: What are the factors and drivers that determine the number of organs donated in New York each year?
questions.guidance: A strong answer frames the problem as an equation: (Terminal patients × % registered donors × organs/donor) + (Terminal patients × % not registered × % family consent × organs/donor) = organs donated. Drivers of terminal patients: population size, age, life spans, medical technology, accidental death rates. Drivers of % registered: awareness, ease of registration, opt-in vs opt-out design, benefits awareness, religious beliefs. Drivers of family consent rate: awareness, religious beliefs, quality of information from doctors at time of grief, assurance organs only harvested after confirmed death. Drivers of organs per person: average number of healthy, usable organs. A great answer adds the implication: only the registration rate and family consent rate are actually controllable by the Commission.

questions.prompt: The team has decided to focus on increasing the number of registered donors and is specifically interested in kidney donations. The Health Commission knows that it needs 9,200 kidneys per year. What percent of New Yorkers need to be registered donors in order for 9,200 kidneys to be donated in a year? (Population: 10 million; % terminally ill/injured per year: 0.1%; % of families that give consent: 10%)
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up and solve algebraically for RD (percent registered donors). Key insight: each person has two kidneys, so the equation targets 4,600 donors (not 9,200). Walk the interviewer through the setup and solution. A great answer notes whether 40% seems reasonable based on real-world intuition.

math.setup: Let RD = percent of New Yorkers who are registered donors. (10,000,000 × 0.001 × RD) + (10,000,000 × 0.001 × 0.1 × (1-RD)) = 4,600
math.answer: RD = 0.40 = 40% (set target at 4,600 because each person has 2 kidneys; 4,600 × 2 = 9,200)

questions.prompt: What are all of the things the Health Commission should consider doing to increase the number of registered donors?
questions.guidance: A strong answer is MECE with discrete named categories and multiple ideas per category. Sample structure: (1) Benchmarking — internal (what works now) and external (other states/countries); (2) Segmentation — identify high-penetration segments to maintain and low-penetration segments to target; (3) Marketing communications — test TV, radio, online, direct mail, word-of-mouth; develop messaging on program awareness, benefits, and safeguards; (4) Distribution/channel optimization — add registration points beyond driver's license (e.g., doctor/hospital visits); change from opt-in to opt-in-with-easy-opt-out or automatic opt-in with explicit opt-out. Answer should demonstrate common sense and sound business judgment.

questions.prompt: Your Engagement Manager has asked you to draw initial conclusions from the segmentation data (Exhibit 1). What would you tell her? Follow-up: Which segment represents the best opportunity to increase registered donors?
questions.guidance: Strong answer calculates penetration rate for each segment (registered donors / population): Caucasian ~47%, African-American ~5%, Hispanic ~10%, Other ~20%. Candidate should reason through pros/cons: Caucasian — largest absolute upside in numbers but already highly penetrated; African-American — very low penetration but small population limits total upside; Hispanic — low penetration (~10%) and large population (2.5M) creates attractive combination. A good answer selects a target for well-reasoned pros/cons; selecting Hispanic is logical but reasoning matters more than the specific choice. Acknowledge risks such as language barriers and cultural differences.

math.setup: Penetration = Registered Donors / Population for each segment
math.answer: Hispanic segment offers best opportunity: low penetration (~10%) combined with large population (2.5M) yields the greatest potential new registrants among under-penetrated groups.

questions.prompt: The team has decided to focus on increasing registration rate among Hispanics. What are some things we can do to increase registrations?
questions.guidance: This question tests creativity. Expect and push with repeated 'What else?' A good answer is a long, diverse list combining standard tactics and creative ideas. Examples: Spanish-language marketing materials and registration forms; community outreach through churches, community centers, and local events; partnerships with Hispanic media (Telemundo, Univision); mobile registration vans in Hispanic neighborhoods; leveraging trusted community leaders/doctors as advocates; social media campaigns in Spanish; integrating registration into healthcare visits; culturally sensitive messaging addressing religious concerns; partnering with Spanish-language employers. Candidate should respond constructively to repeated pressure.

questions.prompt: The head of the Health Commission just walked in and wants a recommendation for what to do to quickly reach Hispanics. What's your recommendation? Start talking now.
questions.guidance: A strong answer is short (~20 seconds), organized, and forceful with no hedging. Structure: synthesize the opportunity, pick 2-3 highest-impact short-term tactics from the brainstorm with brief rationale, and express confidence. Example: 'Clearly, the Hispanic segment offers significant upside given low penetration and large population. I recommend we (1) launch Spanish-language registration at all hospital and doctor visits, (2) partner with Telemundo and community churches for awareness campaigns, and (3) pilot mobile registration vans in high-density Hispanic neighborhoods — these three moves maximize reach and speed at reasonable cost.'

brainstorming.prompt: What are all of the things the Health Commission should consider doing to increase the number of registered donors among Hispanics?

categories.name: Marketing & Awareness
ideas: Spanish-language TV and radio ads (Telemundo, Univision)
Spanish-language digital and social media campaigns
Direct mail in Spanish to Hispanic households
Culturally sensitive messaging addressing religious concerns about donation

categories.name: Registration Channel Expansion
ideas: Add organ donor registration at hospital admissions and doctor visits
Mobile registration vans in high-density Hispanic neighborhoods
Online registration portal in Spanish
Registration at DMV with Spanish-language option prominently offered

categories.name: Community & Influencer Outreach
ideas: Partner with Hispanic community churches and faith leaders
Engage local Hispanic community organizations and nonprofits
Recruit Hispanic physicians and nurses as spokespeople
Leverage word-of-mouth through respected community leaders

categories.name: Cultural & Language Accessibility
ideas: Translate all forms, FAQs, and informational materials into Spanish
Train hospital staff on culturally sensitive conversations with Hispanic families
Develop FAQ specifically addressing common cultural and religious objections
Create testimonial content featuring Hispanic donors and recipients

categories.name: Process & Policy Changes
ideas: Switch to opt-out (automatic registration with explicit opt-out option)
Simplify registration form to reduce friction
Allow family members to register on behalf of a relative
Integrate registration into Medicaid and CHIP enrollment processes

recommendation: Target the Hispanic segment for a concentrated donor-registration push, given its low penetration (~10%) and large population (2.5M) offering the greatest incremental upside among under-penetrated groups

In the short term, launch Spanish-language registration at all healthcare touchpoints, partner with Hispanic media outlets and community faith leaders for awareness, and pilot mobile registration vans in high-density Hispanic neighborhoods
risks: Language and cultural barriers may reduce campaign effectiveness if messaging is not authentically developed with Hispanic community input
Opt-out policy changes require legislative action and public debate, extending timeline
Low baseline trust in the healthcare system among some Hispanic communities may require sustained relationship-building before registration rates improve
next_steps: Conduct focus groups with Hispanic community members to refine messaging and identify key objections
Benchmark registration tactics used in states or countries with high Hispanic donor participation
Pilot 2-3 highest-impact tactics in a single market and measure lift in registration rate before scaling
Build partnerships with Telemundo, Univision, and local Hispanic community organizations
Propose legislative review of opt-out registration policy to maximize long-term impact
